findings.where: Screens 9 (The mystery weight) and 12 (Two unknowns), the typed tasks
findings.what: These are the only typed questions whose words leave out figures they need: screen 9 never says the lower level holds 2 N and 4 N, and screen 12 ("The whole mobile hangs level. What does A weigh?") gives no figures at all. Without the picture, for example in the problem set with new numbers, which shows none, neither can be answered. So write the figures into each task, e.g. screen 12: "A lower bar hangs 15 cm left of the top pivot. A hangs 10 cm left of its string and B 20 cm right. A 6 N weight hangs 15 cm right of the top pivot. The whole mobile hangs level. What does A weigh?"

Only the lower pivot's gauges show, and they still list 2 N × 10 cm and 4 N × 5 cm after the level has folded away, so the cause the screen claims is never on screen: the top bar feels the same 6 N × 20 cm whether the level is folded or not. Show the top pivot's anticlockwise gauge, holding 6 N × 20 cm steady through the fold.

findings.where: The interactive as a whole, and its whatAmILookingAt (shown in the dossier's "What you're looking at")
findings.what: No hook can be dragged on any screen and no mobile has three levels, though the brief promised both, and Dan never balances a two-level mobile himself. The description says "On most screens, a weight or a hook can be dragged" and "one, two or three levels". So either let the hook be dragged on screen 8, or make the description match: weights drag on screens 2, 4 and 6, the pivot on screen 10, with one or two levels.

"A force through the pivot has no distance from it. So it turns nothing." sits loose among the sentences about lower levels. It is the step that explains why the pivot's own string never enters the sum, so tie it to that string: "The string at the pivot pulls up through the pivot. It has no distance from it, so it turns nothing." The brief's "any point may be the pivot" is also left out, and lesson 5's support reactions will need it.

findings.where: Screen 2 text and the explanation's key terms (moment, principle of moments)
findings.what: "This is called its moment" and the amber first-use terms teach the moment and the principle of moments as new, though Dan learned both, and a bar's weight acting at its middle, in Mechanics and materials lesson 2. Recall them in a line ("You know this as its moment") and keep the words for the new ground: folding levels and two unknowns.

findings.where: Screens 1 and 14 (the two pick puzzles), the Why? button
findings.what: Why? shows before Check, and its text ends with the answer ("So the left side goes down", "so the bar stays level"), so one tap skips the prediction. Hide Why? until a Check, as the typed screens already do.

findings.where: Screen 14 picture, right-hand distance labels at 360 px
findings.what: The 6 cm bracket is too short for its label, so "6 cm" sits beyond its end, directly under the 18 cm bracket, and "12 cm" sits off the left end of its own bracket. Each reads as belonging to the wrong span at a glance, so stack the short labels inside their own lanes, or put the 1 N in the outer lane.

findings.where: Screens 4 and 5, the metre rule's printed marks
findings.what: The marks are 12 px in a 340-wide drawing, which comes out at about 10 px on a 360 px phone, below every other label in the lesson (about 11 px). Raise them to 13 px, matching the distance labels.

findings.where: The lead line above every screen
findings.what: "Bars hang on strings, with weights hung along them" sits above the crane (screen 11) and the see-saw (screen 13), where nothing hangs that way, and it takes four lines at 360 px on every screen. Shorten it to "Every weight and distance here is an example."
